title: Canonical strict-tower composition comparison maps
statement:
Let B be a commutative ring. Use the derived categories of strict towers of constant-B module sheaves, their normalized inverse images G and proper direct images R [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], and exact open extension J [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension], with normalized proper/open comparison gamma and cartesian open comparison beta [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. For a compactification c of f:X→Y, with open c.i and proper c.g, put F_c=J_{c.i} followed by R_{c.g}. For a proper refinement r:c→d, with c.i followed by r.hom=d.i and r.hom followed by d.g=c.g, define C_r:F_d→F_c by the identity-left proper/open gamma square, followed by R_{d.g}, inserting the identity and direct-image compositors. Given a cartesian open face from c' to c over x:X'→X and y:Y'→Y with middle map s:c'.Z→c.Z, define E_c:G_y F_c→F_c' G_x by first the proper-square mate and then the open comparison beta, with functor associators inserted.
For f:X→Y and h:Y→Z take a compatible compactification tower T [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower], with c:X→U, b:U→Xbar, i:Y→Ybar open, r:U→Y and p:Xbar→Ybar and q:Ybar→Z proper, b∘c=a, r∘c=f, q∘p the proper part of the compactification of hf, and the cartesian square (b,i,r,p). Set D_T:F_h F_f→F_hf to R_q gamma_(b,i,r,p) J_c with the open and proper compositors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. A refinement of compatible towers consists of refinements w of f, u of h and v of hf satisfying v∘b_1=b_2∘w and p_2∘v=u∘p_1; the individual refinement equations also give w∘c_1=c_2, u∘i_1=i_2, v∘a_1=a_2, r_2∘w=r_1 and q_2∘u=q_1. Its horizontal comparison is H=(C_h F_f1)(F_h2 C_f), with the canonical whiskerings.
A base change of compatible towers is supplied by maps x,y,g on X,Y,Z and middle maps d,t,s on their three compactifications with six cartesian open/proper faces. Apply E to the f, h and hf compactifications to define e_f,e_h,e_hf. Define the horizontal exchange e_h F_f followed by F_h' e_f, with canonical associators. Whenever gamma or beta is used, require quasi-compactness of each of its displayed open immersions, as in the normalized calculus: C requires quasi-compactness of c.i and d.i; E of c.i and c'.i; D of c, i and b; and the whiskered maps require the corresponding source and target open quasi-compactness. F itself imposes no quasi-compactness premise. These are specified natural transformations on the actual derived strict-tower categories; this definition asserts no invertibility, pasting equation or choice-independence theorem.

source.place: Tags 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), compatible-tower comparison construction; 0F7B, 0F7C, 0F7D and 0F7F for refinement and base-change comparisons. The explicit normalized strict-tower maps are the existing constructions extracted from lem-cbc-complete-proetale-composition-pasting-coherence, not a new etale/proetale comparison assertion.

proof.text: Compose J with R to construct F. Normalize the identity-left gamma by rId and rComp to construct C. Compose the proper mate with beta, inserting associators, to construct E. All data are the supplied normalized operations; no witness is chosen.

Use the supplied compatible tower, its cartesian square and its open/proper composition equations to form D. Its formula is the whiskered gamma followed by jComp, jCongr, rComp and equality transport.

Record the three proper refinements and two compatibility equations as CompositionRefinement. Whisker the f comparison and then the h comparison to obtain H. Record the six cartesian faces as CompositionBaseChange. Apply E to each of the three compactifications and form the horizontally pasted exchange by whiskering and associators. These are literal functor-category constructions, with no theorem proof or unproved data.

proof_origin.place: Verbatim extraction of the existing canonical data preceding compositionPastingCoherence; mathematical formulas follow Stacks Tag 0F7J. No new construction or proof obligation. W2: omit the identity components of functor associators and the left unitor in D, C, E and horizontal E; all normalized comparison factors and signatures remain.
